content.text: {"improvements":[{"id":"IMP-001","description":"Move the extensive v1.0→v1.4 changelog narrative from the document header into Appendix D (Change Log) and replace the header with a concise 3-5 line status block. The current header occupies ~150 lines before the TOC and duplicates content already in Appendix D.","rationale":"The header is now larger than several full sections. Reviewers and implementers must scroll past 150+ lines of meta-history to reach the TOC. Consolidating to Appendix D follows standard document hygiene and reduces cognitive load without losing audit history.","location":"Document header (between title and Table of Contents)","priority":"MEDIUM","confidence":0.85},{"id":"IMP-002","description":"Add an explicit format/encoding specification for the `prev_hash` SHA-256 input in §3.2.1 and §5.2.1: state that the canonical content is JCS-serialized as UTF-8 bytes, hashed with SHA-256, and the hex digest is lowercase. Currently §3.2.1 says 'SHA-256 hex of canonical-JSON' but does not specify byte encoding or case.","rationale":"Cross-language hash determinism requires unambiguous byte-level specification. Bash, Python, and Node implementations could diverge on UTF-8 vs UTF-16 BOM handling or hex case, breaking chain verification. The schema pattern `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` implies lowercase but this is not stated normatively.","location":"§3.2.1 (envelope schema prev_hash field), §5.2.1 (audit_emit), §3.3 (canonical serialization paragraph)","priority":"HIGH","confidence":0.88},{"id":"IMP-003","description":"Specify the exact field ordering and inclusion list used for canonicalization input to both prev_hash and signature computation. §3.3 says 'canonical-JSON of prior entry's content (excluding signature + signing_key_id)' but does not enumerate whether `redaction_applied` is included, nor whether field ordering is JCS-sorted (yes, by definition) or struct-defined.","rationale":"JCS canonicalization sorts keys lexicographically, so ordering is deterministic, but the inclusion set must be explicit. If `redaction_applied` is sometimes null and sometimes absent, the canonicalization differs. This ambiguity is the most common source of cross-implementation chain-verification failures.","location":"§3.2.1 schema description, §3.3 data modeling, §5.2.1 audit_emit behavior","priority":"HIGH","confidence":0.9},{"id":"IMP-004","description":"Define behavior when `LOA_AUDIT_KEY_PASSWORD` is set but the key file is unencrypted (or vice versa). §1.7 step 1 lists encrypted-at-rest and plain-key-fallback as alternatives but does not specify what happens on mismatch.","rationale":"Operator misconfiguration (password set but key not encrypted) is a common deployment error. Without a defined fail mode, behavior is implementation-defined and may silently succeed in one runtime and fail in another, producing inconsistent CI behavior.","location":"§1.7 Deployment Architecture, point 1 (per-writer signing key)","priority":"MEDIUM","confidence":0.78},{"id":"IMP-005","description":"Add Sprint 1 acceptance criterion for cross-language JCS conformance: bash `lib/jcs.sh`, Python `rfc8785`, and Node `canonicalize` MUST produce byte-identical output for all vectors in `tests/conformance/jcs/`, verified in CI on Linux + macOS.","rationale":"§2.2 and §3.3 commit to cross-language determinism but Sprint 1 acceptance criteria do not include a CI gate that verifies it. Without an automated check, the three adapters can drift undetected, breaking chain verification across writers using different runtimes.","location":"§8 Sprint 1 launch criteria / acceptance criteria","priority":"HIGH","confidence":0.86},{"id":"IMP-006","description":"Specify rollback/migration behavior for SKP-007 tier_enforcement_mode if the Sprint 1 review flips default from `warn` to `refuse`. Existing operators on unsupported tiers would suddenly fail to boot. Add a one-cycle deprecation grace period or operator-notification mechanism.","rationale":"R19 mitigation says `warn` is the default to avoid blocking operators in production, but the Sprint 1 review may flip to `refuse` per IMP-003. A flip without notice creates a breaking change for any operator on tiers 5+. The `--allow-unsupported-tier` opt-out flag is mentioned but not specified as auto-enabled during transition.","location":"§8 Sprint 1 acceptance criteria SKP-007 paragraph; R19 in §9","priority":"MEDIUM","confidence":0.72},{"id":"IMP-007","description":"Clarify §1.7.1 failure-mode table for L4 trust-ledger conflict: it states git-merge produces `[CHAIN-BROKEN]` and operator runs §3.4.4 recovery, but §3.4.4 recovery walks git history to find a valid prior state, which after a merge would just rewind to pre-merge. Specify whether merged trust-ledger updates are preserved or discarded.","rationale":"The recovery procedure as written would lose any operator B trust transitions that were merged in. This is a data-loss path that should be explicit so operators understand the cost of multi-host violations.","location":"§1.7.1 failure modes table; §3.4.4 hash-chain recovery","priority":"MEDIUM","confidence":0.75},{"id":"IMP-008","description":"Add a concrete schema for the SOUL.md prescriptive-section rejection patterns referenced in §3.2.5 (`.claude/data/lore/agent-network/soul-prescriptive-rejection-patterns.txt`). Currently only 'imperative verbs' are enumerated; the text file is referenced but its format is undefined.","rationale":"L7 schema validation correctness depends on this pattern file. Without a defined format (regex per line? glob? structured YAML?), Sprint 7 implementation will need to invent a format mid-sprint, risking drift from the stated SDD intent.","location":"§3.2.5 SOUL.md schema, validation rejects bullet","priority":"LOW","confidence":0.7},{"id":"IMP-009","description":"Specify the benchmark methodology for SKP-004 worst-case payload latency: warm vs cold cache, ajv compile included or excluded, signing key already loaded vs loaded per-call, and whether the 1000 iterations are sequential or include concurrency.","rationale":"Without methodology specification, the measured p95/p99 numbers are not comparable across runs or platforms. CI variance on macOS runners is notoriously high; benchmark methodology must specify warmup iterations and statistical handling (e.g., trimmed mean vs raw p95) to produce a meaningful SLO revision.","location":"§8 Sprint 1 acceptance criteria SKP-004 paragraph","priority":"MEDIUM","confidence":0.82},{"id":"IMP-010","description":"Resolve the version inconsistency: header says PRD v1.3 (2026-05-02), Appendix B references PRD v1.3 (2026-05-02), but document title says 'v1.4 Flatline pass #3 HIGH_CONSENSUS integration'. Confirm which PRD version v1.4 SDD is anchored to and whether any PRD-side changes are pending.","rationale":"Version coupling between PRD and SDD is load-bearing for the cycle's audit trail. If the SDD claims pass-3 integration but the PRD has not been re-baselined, downstream readers cannot tell whether PRD-level concerns (SKP-002) have been propagated symmetrically.","location":"Header PRD Reference line; Appendix B References","priority":"LOW","confidence":0.6}],"summary":"10 improvements identified, 3 HIGH priority"}
